Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of lumbar strain and
localized low back pain radiating to the paraspinal muscles. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the
kind and force of the collision, and the presenting symptoms align well with that mechanism. Over the course of 19
visits, treatment followed a conventional and expected progression, including manual therapy, therapeutic exercise,
and home stretching guidance. Visit frequency decreased steadily as functional capacity and pain levels improved.
Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury to the lumbar region. No prior injury to
the same body area is known from the patient's history or available records. Billing for services rendered reflects
single, appropriate charges for each documented intervention, with no repeated or duplicate entries. At discharge, the
patient was improving with a good prognosis for full recovery, and a home exercise program was provided for
ongoing self-management.
